basis.governing_question: How can Metalúrgica Norte cut conversion cost across its six plants in Portugal and Spain and put the improvements in place in every plant?

sub_questions.question: Where does conversion cost per part sit in each plant today, and what drives it?
Which improvements, sized per plant, cut conversion cost per part by a measurable amount in every plant?
Do the approved improvements show savings in the cost data at the pilot plant?
How are the improvements put in place in the other plants so they are running in all six plants?
What conversion cost per part does each plant show against its baseline once the improvements run?

drivers.evidence: six plants in Portugal and Spain

work.unit: Site diagnosed on the floor (cost baseline, line observation, loss analysis)

phase_work.why: Three plants diagnosed two at a time, the other three extended from data; above typical 3-6 weeks because three plants need two rounds.

work.unit: Pilot site: changes made and savings shown in the cost data
Rollout wave of up to 3 sites
Conversion cost per part measured after the last wave goes live

phase_work.why: Pilot, two waves in sequence, then a window after wave 2 (earlier windows overlap the next wave); above typical 8-16 weeks: work adds up.

sizing.levers: Running the two rollout waves side by side would cut the most; diagnosing two plants instead of three saves about two weeks.

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish where conversion cost per part arises in each plant and size the improvements that would reduce it.

gate.label: Initiative go/no-go
gate.decision: Go or no-go on the sized improvements, and which plant pilots them first?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Carry out the approved improvements at a pilot plant, roll them out to the other plants, and track savings.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the final results and the running improvements in all six plants?

architect_notes: The brief gives no engagement length, so the 30 to 34 weeks are an estimate from the work sizing, not a stated length.
Implementation takes the middle of a 20 to 30 week estimate; 12-week pilot, 6-week waves and a 6-week window would push it to the top.
Diagnostic assumes three representative plants are diagnosed on the floor and the other three extended from data; which plants is open.
No Measurement phase: a savings window after the last wave runs inside Implementation, so tracking beyond it needs the partner's decision.
